title: Cell complexes, fundamental groups and covering spaces
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: Cell complexes, fundamental groups and covering spaces in the form used by the courses of the programme on group rings and classifying spaces. The first lesson proves that complexes built by attaching cells are Hausdorff and closure-finite, that collapsing a contractible subcomplex and changing attaching maps by homotopies preserve the homotopy type, that trees are contractible and connected graphs have spanning trees, and that finite two-complexes whose cells are attached along closed walks can be triangulated, with simplicial approximation in carrier form. The second proves that the fundamental group of a graph is the group of walks up to backtracking, by unwinding the graph into the tree of its reduced walks, with a free basis from a spanning tree; that attaching 2-cells divides the fundamental group by the normal subgroup generated by the attaching loops and higher cells change nothing; and that presentation complexes carry the presented group and every two-complex is homotopy equivalent to one. The third treats universal covers of cell complexes with their lifted cells and deck transformations, the lifting criterion, covers for normal subgroups, the lifting of homotopy equivalences, cellular chains of covers as free modules over the group ring with the boundary formula for cells attached along closed walks, subcomplexes and their universal covers, and the Cayley complex of a presentation with its Fox derivatives.
prerequisites: core course Algebraic Topology (D60), edition with Roberts's lectures and Fomberg's components: Lecture 4 Definition 4.4; Lecture 5 Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 5.3; Lecture 6 Definition 6.2; Lecture 7 Proposition 7.1, Definition 7.1, Lemma 7.1 and Corollary 7.1; Lecture 9 Corollaries 9.1 and 9.4; Lecture 10 Theorem 10.1 and Corollary 10.1; Lecture 12 Example 12.2 and Corollary 12.1; Lecture 16 Definition 16.1, Propositions 16.1 and 16.2 and Corollary 16.1; Lecture 17 Lemma 17.1; Lecture 18 Lemma 18.2 and Proposition 18.2; Fomberg component 7 (lemma on skeleta, cellular homology theorem (14.1)-(14.2), incidence formula with (15.3)); Fomberg Theorem 1.13 and Corollary 1.14

checks.reading: Classical material, written independently on the providers of the programme: the core course Algebraic Topology (Roberts's lectures on the fundamental groupoid, Seifert-van Kampen and covering spaces; Fomberg's components on singular and cellular homology with the edition's repairs), the lessons Grassmannians and classifying maps and Frame fields and primary obstructions of the course on characteristic classes, and the lesson Words, free groups and Cayley graphs. Hatcher, Algebraic Topology (author's page; free shelf copy), is cited as further reading; its Propositions 0.16-0.18, 1.26, 1A.1, 1A.2, 1.33, 1.34, 1.39, 4.1, Theorem 2.35 and Theorem 2C.1 were located in the free copy on 16 Oct 2026. Changes of form against Hatcher: the fundamental group of a graph is computed by the covering tree of reduced walks and the fibre bijection of the core course, not by collapsing a maximal tree and a many-set van Kampen theorem; attaching cells uses the two-set van Kampen theorem of the core course, induction and a compactness argument; the cellular boundary formula for cells along closed walks is derived from the incidence formula of the core course and the comparison of paths and chains.
